text:
jane_acme: Hey team — we've started seeing intermittent errors from the embeddings endpoint after upgrading our client lib. Sometimes we get a 400 with "embedding dimension mismatch", other times a 504 gateway timeout. Happening only in production (high throughput). Using the Python SDK to batch 8 texts at once. Any ideas?

alex_support: Sorry to hear that, we'll help dig in. Can you paste: model name, SDK versions (Python/TS/Go if you use any), a minimal repro, and a sample raw error (including request_id if present)? Also are you hitting any 429s?

jane_acme: Model: embed-fast-768 (we thought it was 768 dim). Python SDK v0.11.0. TS SDK in another service also v0.11.0. We only see the dimension error when batch > 1. Sample Python code we call in prod:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
texts = ["doc1...", "doc2...", "doc3...", "doc4..."]
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-fast-768", input=texts)
print(resp)
```Error snippet from logs:```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "error": "embedding dimension mismatch: received vector length 1536 but model expects 768",
  "request_id": "req_ABC123"
}
```Also sometimes we see: `504 Gateway Timeout` and a few `429` backoffs.

alex_support: Thanks. Two starting hypotheses: 1) the model on the server is actually a 1536-dim model (alias mismatch), or 2) the SDK is serializing batched inputs incorrectly such that the server interprets arrays as precomputed embeddings (so it tries to validate lengths). A couple quick checks: - If you call the embeddings endpoint with a single input (batch_size=1 / only one text) do you get a valid embedding back? - Can you run a curl that prints request/response headers (we need the X-Redwood-Request-ID and Content-Type payload).

jane_acme: Single input works fine (I tried 1 text locally). The failures reproduce when we send lists length >=2. Here's curl we ran from our CI when it failed (obfuscated):```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-fast-768","input":["a","b"]}'
```Response headers included `X-Redwood-Request-ID: req_ABC123`. Body same as above.

sam_eng: FYI there's been a couple model alias updates in the last quarter where some older aliases now point to a 1536 unified embedding under the hood to improve quality. That could explain the 1536 dims. But it doesn't explain why single-input works and multi-input breaks. Could be an SDK bug in how it encodes the JSON for batch arrays.

maria_sre: I pulled logs for req_ABC123 on the infra side. When we received the request the server saw Content-Length 452, Content-Type application/json. The payload we received looked like this (scrubbed): ```json
{"model":"embed-fast-768","input":[[0.12,0.34,...],[0.45,0.11,...]]}
```Which indicates the client may have sent precomputed vectors (2 arrays) rather than an array of strings. That explains the dimension error — server validated vector length 1536 vs model 768. Can you confirm your application didn't transform text into embeddings client-side?

jane_acme: Whoa — we do have a microservice that occasionally attempts local embedding caching with `sentence-transformers` and will short-circuit the request by sending cached vectors to Redwood for normalization. But we thought we only sent raw text. We do not intentionally convert to vectors in this flow. Could an SDK change have caused text arrays to be encoded as numeric arrays?

tim_ml: Two things to check: 1) If your cache path returned a numpy array and you accidentally passed that into the SDK's `input` list, JSON encoder could indeed produce numeric arrays. 2) There was a known bug in Python SDK v0.11.0 where objects implementing the buffer protocol (numpy arrays) were auto-converted during serialization instead of being rejected. That caused some callers to send numeric arrays. The fix is in v0.12.1 where we validate `input` types and raise a clear error. Workarounds: - upgrade SDK to >= v0.12.1 - explicitly cast items to `str` before calling `client.embeddings.create(...)` - disable client-side batching for the cache path for now.

jane_acme: Ok that matches: our cache returns `np.array` when the vector exists and we append it into the same list as text. So sometimes `input` becomes `["text1", array([...])]` which gets serialized as `["text1", [0.1,0.2,...]]`. That would make the server think you supplied embeddings for the second item. Two follow-ups: 1) Why did single-input calls work? Because when only text items are present there's no array. 2) Why timeout/504 sometimes? Possibly larger payloads or gateway timeouts when server tries to validate large numeric arrays.

alex_support: Thanks for the detective work — that explains the dimension error. For the 504/429s we should still check retries/timeouts. Recommended immediate actions (short term):
- Sanitize inputs before calling SDK: ensure every element in `input` is a string. Example in Python:```python
clean_inputs = [s if isinstance(s, str) else json.dumps(s) if isinstance(s, (dict, list)) else str(s) for s in inputs]
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-fast-768", input=clean_inputs)
```- Upgrade Python/TS SDK to >= v0.12.1 which rejects numeric arrays and gives clearer errors. - If you must batch mixed cached vectors/text, split the call paths: send precomputed vectors via the dedicated vector endpoint (if supported) or normalize them locally to strings first.

maria_sre: For the timeouts: add retries with exponential backoff and a 30s request timeout. Example pseudo-retry:```python
import time
for attempt in range(5):
  try:
    resp = client.embeddings.create(..., timeout=30)
    break
  except (TimeoutError, ServerError) as e:
    sleep = (2 ** attempt) + random.random()
    time.sleep(sleep)
    continue
```We also applied a temporary rate-limit burst policy for your team while you stabilize — you'll see slightly higher 429s if you exceed burst.

sam_eng: Also check model alias mapping: run this quick check to inspect the returned embedding length with a single known input to verify model dims:```python
r = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-fast-768", input=["test"]) 
print(len(r.data[0].embedding))
# expected 768
```If you get 1536, switch to `embed-lite-768` or contact us for alias remap.

jane_acme: I ran that and got 1536 — so alias points to unified 1536. We're going to switch to `embed-lite-768` for the short term. We'll also sanitize inputs and upgrade the SDK. One last question: should we open a ticket for a server-side validation improvement to catch mixed-type input arrays earlier?

alex_support: Yes please open a support ticket and include the raw request bodies (scrub API keys) and request IDs (e.g., req_ABC123). We'll flag it to runtime + SDK teams for a postmortem on making error messages clearer. I'll also create an internal bug for the SDK team to ensure mixed-type arrays get a documented error in release notes.

oncall_bot: Notice: we deployed a small serialization validation change to the ingestion layer at 2025-11-12T02:14Z that will start rejecting numeric arrays for `input` in a stricter mode for older SDKs. Some callers may receive clearer 400s instead of ambiguous 504s.

jane_acme: Thanks everyone — will do the upgrades and report back. :thumbsup:
